subject: green caterpillar
title: This Caterpillar Shoots Its Poop 38 Body Lengths to Stay Alive

scenes.text: A caterpillar fires its own poop five feet through the air. It has a good reason.
The silver-spotted skipper caterpillar lives inside a little tent of folded leaf, across most of the United States.
When it has to go, it builds up pressure, then flicks the pellet off a tiny comb on its rear end.
The pellet flies up to 38 times the caterpillar's body length. Scaled up to a person, that's more than 200 feet.
Biologists found out why. Hunting wasps follow the smell of droppings straight to a caterpillar's shelter.
So it never keeps the evidence at home. It launches it.

description:
The silver-spotted skipper caterpillar shoots its own droppings up to 38 times its body length.
The caterpillar (Epargyreus clarus), found across most of the United States and into southern Canada, lives in a shelter it builds from a folded leaf. Instead of leaving its droppings (frass) there, it raises the blood pressure in its rear end and launches each pellet off a structure called an anal comb. A 4 cm caterpillar has been measured firing a pellet 153 cm, about 38 body lengths; for a human that would be more than 200 feet. Biologist Martha Weiss (Ecology Letters, 2003) showed why: predatory wasps are attracted to the smell of frass, and caterpillars close to frass were particularly vulnerable to wasp attack, while living with their own waste did the caterpillars no harm.
Which animal has the strangest defence you know? Comment below.
